acme_dev: Hey team — after upgrading our embed client to the latest internal lib we started getting intermittent 400s from /v1/embeddings. Only happens on bulk requests.
laura.support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact request payload (sanitized API key) and the error body you see?
acme_dev: sure, here's an anonymized curl we used (we gzip on the fly):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ****" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-ndjson" \
  -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" \
  --data-binary @embeds.ndjson.gz
```
embeds.ndjson (first two lines):
```
["single sentence example"]
["second sentence example"]
```
acme_dev: Response body we get: 
```json
{"error":"invalid_input_shape","message":"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 768 (line 1)"}
```
mateo.eng: quick guess — when using NDJSON each line should be a JSON object or array per the embeddings API, not a top-level JSON array on a single line. Your example shows a string-wrapped array on each line. Can you show the raw un-gzipped bytes for the first few lines?
acme_dev: here's raw (hex snippet): `5b2268656c6c6f222c20226869` — that decodes to `["hello", "hi"` on single line. We thought NDJSON allowed arrays per line.
laura.support: NDJSON allows any JSON value per line, but our embeddings endpoint expects either a top-level array (for application/json) or per-line JSON object `{"input": "..."}` for NDJSON. Sending a bare JSON array with strings yields ambiguous shape for the server-side parser which then infers dimension incorrectly.
eng-ml: Echoing — we recently tightened the input shape checks. Server will attempt to parse: if it sees a string scalar it treats as single item of default dim (768) for some models; if it sees an array it tries to parse an already-computed vector. The payload you sent looks like a stringified array rather than a proper `{"input": "..."}` object per line.
acme_dev: oh hmm. The old client used to send `["a","b"]` as a single request body (application/json) for batch. We switched to NDJSON + gzip to stream. Maybe our serializer wraps each input as JSON.stringify(input) and that produces a string on each line.
mateo.eng: Can you reproduce locally with this minimal curl to remove gzip complexity?
```bash
printf '%s\n' '{"input":"first"}' '{"input":"second"}' > test.ndjson
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ****" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-ndjson" \
  --data-binary @test.ndjson
```
acme_dev: running that now... getting 200 and two embeddings.
acme_dev: so that works. If I instead do `printf '%s\n' '["first"]' '["second"]'` I get the 400.
laura.support: that nails it — your serializer is emitting JSON arrays (strings) as top-level values per line, which our parser treats differently. Two mitigation paths:
- Fix client to emit per-line objects: `{"input": <string>}`.
- Or send a single application/json payload where the top-level is an array of strings (i.e., `[{"a"},{"b"}]`).
eng-ml: also watch out for BOM/encoding and double-stringification. We saw cases where libraries `JSON.stringify` twice ended up sending `"[\"a\"]"` (a string containing JSON), which makes shape detection yield wrong dims. If you see quotes around the leading `[` in raw bytes, that's double-stringified.
acme_dev: Ah yes, I can see in our logs we call `line = JSON.stringify(item)` and then push `line` to stream — for objects that worked but for arrays the stringify results in `"[... ]"`. So line becomes a JSON string not a JSON array.
laura.support: That explains the dimension 768 fallback — the server took the string, hashed it differently, or attempted a legacy embedding path.
mateo.eng: Quick patch suggestion (Node):
```js
// BAD
stream.write(JSON.stringify(item) + '\n')
// GOOD
const line = typeof item === 'string' ? JSON.stringify({ input: item }) : JSON.stringify(item)
stream.write(line + '\n')
```
acme_dev: patching now. Also curious — we saw a billing spike when these 400s started. Any idea?
laura.support: if clients retry aggressively on 4xx instead of backing off, retries can multiply billable token/requests. Also if your code switched from batching N items per request to N singleline requests because of serialization bug, requests count went up. We can pull your usage logs to confirm.
support-bot: Noted: raised support ticket #SUP-2026 and flagged for billing review.
eng-ml: follow-up: we'll add a clearer error message for this case in the runtime that says: "invalid NDJSON element: expected object with \u0022input\u0022 or top-level array for JSON; got stringified JSON."
laura.support: For now, once you fix the serializer you should be green. If you want, paste the failing raw gz file and we can decode and confirm the exact byte sequence.
acme_dev: sending sample gz file link (private) to the thread DM. Thanks all, patching and will report back. :thumbsup:
mateo.eng: awesome — once you confirm fixed we'll close the ticket. If you hit weird latency after switching from one big JSON to NDJSON+gzip, note that gzip overhead + many small requests can increase CPU on our ingress leading to transient latency; batching multiple inputs per line/object is still the best perf/cost.
acme_dev: re-tested with patched serializer and NDJSON objects — everything OK (200, dims 1536). Thanks!
laura.support: great. Closing loop in 24h if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
